Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address City Council, please complete a speaker card and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public
comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote and on matters not listed on the
agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council: Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are
available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the
agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has
been posted will also be made available for public inspection. Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City
Clerk’s Department, during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.,
every other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at
recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

RECESS

City Council recessed at 6:04 p.m. pending the commencement of the regular meeting.

  REGULAR MEETING

Mayor Ayala called the meeting to order at 6:10 p.m. in the Council Chambers, Norwalk
City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. City Council was present in its
entirety with Councilmembers Ramirez, Rios, and Valencia, Vice Mayor Perez, and Mayor
Ayala responding to roll call. Also present were Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager;
Arnold M. Alvarez, City Attorney; and Theresa Devoy, City Clerk.

The invocation was delivered by Arthur McKibben, La Mirada Church of the Nazarene;
followed by the flag salute, led by Isabella Villegas, Foundation Christian School.

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

Councilmember Ramirez requested the meeting be adjourned in memory of Pastor
Reggie Bowie. Councilmember Rios thanked first responders and the community for
supporting the wildfire victims; reported on her attendance at the Las Posadas event
where they also conducted a Toy Giveaway and thanked Ken Cook, Norwalk High School
Race Team, Dream Big Project, McKinney-Vento Program, Norwalk-La Mirada Unified
School District (NLMUSD), Motivated Landscape, Rios Family, and So Cal Barbers;
congratulated the 605 All-Star Band on their participation in the Tournament of Roses
Parade; reported on her attendance at the City of Norwalk’s First Responders Toy
Giveaway; toured the Veterans Villas with Senator Bob Archuleta, and visited the Senior
Center. Councilmember Valencia reported on her attendance at a Norwalk Lions Club
International event, McKinney-Vento Toy Giveaway, the 605 All-Star Band practice, the
Las Posadas event , and met with a resident regarding community concerns; shared that
the Shree Pashupatinath Foundation donated many essential items for wildfire victims
and thanked Rameshor Bhandari for aiding in the assistance; recognized members of the
Norwalk Community Emergency Response Team for also assisting in the wildfire
disaster; and announced Norwalk is partnering with Norwalk Lions Club International for
a Food Distribution event being held January 25 at the Los Angeles County Recorder’s
parking lot. Vice Mayor Perez reported on her attendance at the United Parents Club
Dance, City of Norwalk’s First Responders Toy Giveaway; thanked all who participated
in the Santa Sleigh program; and attended the California Contract Cities Association
Legislative Tour in Sacramento to discuss Proposition 36, other various topics were
discussed such as housing policies and homeless encampments.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

The City Attorney indicated there was no reportable action taken on the matters discussed
in closed session.

Background:

On February 5, 2024 staff issued an invitation for bids for the construction of Project No. 7235
– Intelligent Transportation Systems Improvement along Imperial Highway from San Gabriel
River to Shoemaker Avenue. Work at the City Maintenance Yard and Traffic Operations
Center (TOC) was added to this project.

The project along Imperial Highway includes traffic signal and ITS improvements, such as
installing signal cabinets, service enclosures, conduit, traffic poles and mast arms, luminaires,
vehicle and pedestrian signal heads, accessible push buttons, video detection systems, closed
circuit television (CCTV) cameras, fiber optic cable, advanced controllers, malfunction
monitoring units, and ethernet switches. Work at the City Maintenance Yard involves installing
conduit, fiber optic cable, splice vaults, and a fiber distribution unit, and integrating the
upgraded controller into the existing Centracs Advanced Traffic Management System (ATMS).
Additionally, Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) ramps along the corridor are being
reconstructed.

At Imperial Highway and Hoxie Avenue, improvements include constructing a 12' right turn bay
in the westbound direction, reconstructing the ADA ramp, sidewalk, curb, gutter, catch basin,
and asphalt concrete, and installing a new concrete collar to connect the catch basin to the
existing pipe. The northwest pedestrian ramp is also being upgraded to ADA standards. Traffic
signal modifications include new poles, pull boxes, and conduit, along with signing and striping
updates.

SUBJECT: AMENDMENT NO. 7 TO THE AGREEMENT FOR BUS STOP MAINTENANCE
  SERVICES

Background:

On March 31, 2008, the City entered into an agreement with Nationwide Environmental Services
Inc. (NES), a Division of Joe’s Sweeping Inc. to perform bus stop maintenance services.

NES maintains 192 citywide bus stops and four canopies located at the Metrolink Transportation
Center. Locations are categorized based on the amenities at the bus stops and cleaning
frequencies range from daily to weekly, depending on high traffic locations and need. Cleaning
includes removal of trash and replacement of trash liners, graffiti removal, deodorizing of
shelters, and pressure washing of benches and hardscapes.

Several amendments to the agreement have previously been approved to extend the term,
adjust compensation, etc. In February 2022, Amendment No. 6 was approved to increase the
term to twelve (12) years with one-year automatic renewals effective July 1, 2022, and modify
the provision regarding the annual Consumer Price Index (CPI) adjustment to remove the 5%
cap.

NES has gone beyond the scope of the contract by maintaining a higher cleaning frequency
without additional cost to the City. However, due to growing vandalism, it has become necessary
to amend their contract to better address the following issues:

  1. Increased Traffic and Public Usage: The City's bus stops have seen a significant rise
  in foot traffic, resulting in a quicker buildup of litter and requiring more frequent cleaning
  to maintain cleanliness and functionality.
  2. Non-Transit Riders: Bus stops experience high usage by a variety of individuals,
  including those without stable housing. As a result, these locations require increased
 City Council  February 4, 2025
Amendment No. 7 to Bus Stop Maintenance Services  Page No. 2

  maintenance efforts to ensure they remain clean, safe, and accessible for all members of
  the public.
  3. Improper Trash Disposal: Individuals occasionally use the bus stop receptacles for
  household trash disposal, which overwhelms the bins' intended capacity.
  4. Trash Spillage: In some cases, people digging through the trash spill its contents,
  leaving the area in disarray and creating additional cleaning needs.

Given these circumstances, City staff requested a quote from NES to help the City address these
concerns. NES responded and proposed additional services with an increase in cleaning
frequency as described in Exhibit A (attached), to address these growing challenges. The current
monthly cost is $19,697. The increase in service frequency would cost an additional $8,300
(42%) per month, for a new monthly expenditure of $27,997 for the remaining five months of FY
2024/25. These services would commence March 1, 2025.

Additionally, NES is requesting to modify Section 2.3, Payment Adjustment, in which they would
modify the CPI provision based on the CPI index for February of each year or 4%, whichever is
greater. This modification would aid in the management of rising operational costs, including
labor, insurance, fuel, and parts, ensuring the long-term sustainability of the contract.

budget under the Prop C budget.

SUBJECT: PERSONNEL APPEALS BOARD CERTIFIED LIST

Background:

Norwalk Municipal Code (NMC) §2.24.110 provides that City Council shall establish a list of five
people who may serve on a Personnel Appeals Board as needed. A Personnel Appeals Board
is convened whenever necessary to hear an appeal pursuant to the grievance procedure
established in the NMC. Whenever an appeal is filed, three members from the established list
are selected by the Mayor to hear the appeal; the selections are subject to approval by the entire
City Council. Each person on the list of potential Personnel Appeals Board members shall be
selected based upon their experience in the area of personnel relations. The NMC also provides
that each name on the list shall remain certified as a potential Board member until such person
resigns or a majority of the City Council determines to remove such name. Periodically, the list
is brought before City Council for review and/or if there is a vacancy.

Currently, there are three individuals who comprise the list: Kim Apodaca (Perez), Olga Avina
(Rios), and Gloria Rodriguez (Ayala). Councilmembers Ramirez and Valencia have vacancies
and staff is recommending that appointments be made in order to have a complete list of five
individuals that could be called upon if there was a need to convene a Personnel Appeals Board
to hear a matter.
